recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中央一顆漿細胞的細胞質塞滿數十個淡藍色、圓形的球狀包涵體（Russell bodies），把核擠到一旁，看起來像一串葡萄；這就是 Mott 細胞，周圍是成熟嗜中性球。
features: Single plasma cell with cytoplasm packed by numerous round, pale blue, refractile globules (Russell bodies)
Globules of fairly uniform size, giving a grape-cluster or mulberry appearance
Nucleus partly obscured and displaced by the inclusions
Surrounding mature segmented neutrophils and band forms
Background red cells and scattered myeloid precursors; smear has a bluish color cast
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a plasma cell whose cytoplasm is distended by numerous round, uniform, pale blue globular inclusions (Russell bodies), displacing and partially obscuring the nucleus, surrounded by mature neutrophils and band forms. These inclusions represent accumulated, incompletely secreted immunoglobulin. Mott cells are not specific for neoplasia and occur in reactive plasmacytosis, but in the context of a clonal plasma cell proliferation the findings are consistent with plasma cell myeloma with Mott cell morphology.

ddx.vs: Mott cells also occur in reactive conditions, so clonality must be established by kappa/lambda restriction and plasma cell percentage rather than by the inclusions themselves.
Macrophages have abundant pale cytoplasm with heterogeneous debris and a reniform nucleus, not uniform homogeneous globules in a plasma cell.
Pseudo-Chediak-Higashi granules are large azurophilic/eosinophilic granules in myeloid blasts rather than pale blue immunoglobulin globules in a plasma cell.

ddx.dx: Vacuolated plasma cells or lymphoma cells
ddx.vs: Empty lipid or artifact vacuoles appear clear rather than as pale blue, solid, refractile globules.
